title: Cline vs Continue
summary: Compare IDE coding assistants by model control, permission behavior and upstream maintenance evidence.

sections.heading: Resolve the maintenance question first
paragraphs: Continue's upstream repository says it is read-only and no longer actively maintained. Verify the exact extension or CLI package, publisher, update channel and security response before including it in a supported production shortlist.

sections.heading: Test permission and model paths
paragraphs: Use the same repository task and model provider where possible. Record which actions require approval, where inference runs, what credentials are needed and which external services receive code or prompts.

sections.heading: Treat local inference as a separate test
paragraphs: Both profiles contain model-configuration information, but configuration support does not prove that a particular local model will meet quality, latency or hardware needs. Test a representative change and inspect the resulting diff.

pros.text: Cline documents local STDIO and remote MCP servers and supports server management in its IDE extension and CLI.
Continue documents configurable MCP servers as custom tools in Agent mode.

cons.text: Continue's documentation limits MCP use to Agent mode, so this capability is not documented across all modes.
Continue's upstream repository says it is read-only and no longer actively maintained; its package and support path need confirmation.

faqs.question: Can Continue use MCP outside Agent mode?
faqs.answer: No. Continue's MCP documentation says MCP tools are available only in Agent mode.

faqs.question: Which MCP transport does Cline recommend?
faqs.answer: Cline marks Streamable HTTP as recommended and SSE as legacy; match the transport to the server you intend to use.

verdict: Cline and Continue should not be treated as equivalent maintenance choices today: Continue's upstream read-only notice is a decision-critical caveat. Verify distribution and support before evaluating feature fit.
bestFor: Developers deciding how much model configuration and maintenance risk they can own
notFor: Teams that require a current upstream support commitment without first checking the package lifecycle
migration: Pin the current package version, export model configuration and preserve a working fallback. Reassess extension publisher and update state before each upgrade.
gaps: Continue package distribution, publisher, security response and current support lifecycle require confirmation.
No local-model quality, privacy or performance trial has been performed.
